methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective cohort of 300 FIGO IIB-IVA LACC patients, with 1:1 PSM (caliper 0.1 SD) yielding 240 matched patients and SMDs<0.05. Statistical analyses are extensive and appropriate: multivariable Cox with Schoenfeld residuals, RCS dose-response modeling, IPW sensitivity analysis, MICE for missing data, interaction tests, and post-hoc power analysis. However, the underlying allocation is non-random and driven by tumor characteristics (bulky tumors or MRI parametrial invasion preferentially received 3D-PTIB), creating systematic confounding by indication that PSM cannot fully remove. There is also a fundamental imaging-modality asymmetry: 3D-PTIB used CT+MRI, while F-3DIB used intraoperative CT only, confounding target volume definition and D90 comparisons.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective individual cohort with propensity matching corresponds to Oxford LoE 2b. The clinical question (3D-printed template vs freehand interstitial brachytherapy in LACC) is highly relevant for improving local control and reducing late toxicity, especially in bulky/parametrial-invasion subgroups. The reported ~11% absolute LC gain and >50% reduction in grade 3 proctitis are clinically meaningful, though confirmation requires prospective multicenter validation.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is applicable. Inclusion/exclusion flow is well described, PSM procedure and covariates are detailed, and dosimetric and toxicity outcomes are reported with CIs. Several reporting weaknesses: acknowledged selection bias by allocation protocol, acknowledged imaging modality asymmetry that complicates D90 comparisons, exploratory secondary endpoints not adjusted for multiplicity (authors note this), time-to-toxicity not systematically recorded, and no data/code availability statement. Figures are limited (only 2 described), and the extended statistical section is somewhat disorganized with redundant text.

novelty_literature.justification: 3D-printed templates for interstitial brachytherapy in cervical cancer have been studied (Logar 2019, Marar 2022), and the EMBRACE-I and hybrid ICBT/ISBT literature establish dose-response relationships. The novelty here is the relatively large (n=240 matched) real-world comparison with 3-year follow-up, inclusion of survival endpoints, RCS-based dose-response modeling identifying a plateau near 85 Gy, and subgroup analyses by tumor size/parametrial invasion. This is a meaningful incremental extension rather than a conceptual breakthrough.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is detailed and generally readable, with a thorough methods section describing the template fabrication workflow and contingency planning. Weaknesses include an extremely long and partially redundant statistical methods paragraph, inconsistent hyphenation ('3D-printed template-guided interstitial brachytherapy' repeated verbatim many times), some repetition in the discussion, and only two figures described (flowchart and treatment protocols) without dosimetric or survival curves. Tables are adequately captioned.

key_strengths: Large PSM cohort (240 matched patients) with 3-year follow-up showing significant OS and LC benefits for 3D-PTIB
Robust statistical toolkit: Cox with Schoenfeld residuals, RCS for dose-response, IPW sensitivity analysis, MICE for missingness
Subgroup analysis and formal interaction tests demonstrating benefit concentrated in bulky tumors (>4 cm) and parametrial invasion
Clinically meaningful reduction in grade 3+ radiation proctitis (4.2% vs 11.7%) with concurrent target dose escalation
key_concerns: Non-random allocation driven by tumor characteristics; confounding by indication may remain despite PSM
Systematic imaging asymmetry (CT+MRI for 3D-PTIB vs intraoperative CT for F-3DIB) complicates D90 and HR-CTV comparisons
Multiplicity not corrected for secondary endpoints (PFS p=0.05, subgroup analyses) - authors label these exploratory
Time-to-toxicity not recorded; limited figure set (no survival curves or dose-response plot shown)
Single-center retrospective design without external validation; no data/code availability
chief_reviewer.rationale: A clinically meaningful, statistically thorough, but single-center retrospective comparison with clear allocation bias and imaging asymmetry; suitable for a mid-tier oncology or radiotherapy journal after minor revisions for figures, multiplicity discussion, and clarity.
